correctness.rationale: A clustered exponential determinant has a nonzero leading Vandermonde coefficient. Hence a selected maximal minor is a nontrivial real-analytic function in either delays or angles, and the standard analytic zero-set theorem makes the rank-deficient set measure zero. Rectangular, boundary-angle, and clustered-conditioning cases were checked.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Ng--Kutz source still states the generalized-Vandermonde rank property as Conjecture 1 and conditions its nonuniform stable-embedding result on it. Searches found no later source-specific resolution. Standard analytic-zero-set and Vandermonde tools are not claimed as new; limited full-text access is recorded as residual risk.

value.rationale: The result removes the explicit rank conjecture for absolutely continuous uneven-delay laws even with system frequencies fixed, while the clustered-delay asymptotic proves that almost-sure rank does not solve finite-sample conditioning.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
